definitions.explanation: The lowest rank in the Japanese peerage system ({華族|かぞく}) established in 1884 and abolished in 1947. Also used as the general translation for the European title of baron.
Short for {男爵|だんしゃく}いも, a popular variety of potato in Japan with a floury texture, well-suited for mashing and croquettes. Named after Baron Kawata, who introduced it to Hokkaido.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{男爵|だんしゃく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{称号|しょうごう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っていた→持つ：00478_motsu⟧。
examples.english: He held the title of baron.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明治時代|めいじじだい}→明治時代：28080_meijijidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{華族|かぞく}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{作|つく}られ→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧、{男爵|だんしゃく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{低|ひく}い→低い：02947_hikui⟧{位|くらい}だった。
examples.english: The peerage system was created in the Meiji era, with baron being the lowest rank.

examples.japanese: ⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ドイツ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{男爵|だんしゃく}{家|け}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{末裔|まつえい}⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{設定|せってい}→設定：04767_settei⟧だ。
examples.english: The novel's protagonist is set up as a descendant of a German baronial family.

examples.japanese: {男爵|だんしゃく}いも⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦コロッケ→コロッケ：10857_korokke⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made croquettes with baron potatoes.

examples.japanese: {男爵|だんしゃく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ほくほく⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦ポテトサラダ→ポテトサラダ：27703_potetosarada⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}いている→向く：02304_muku⟧。
examples.english: Baron potatoes are floury, so they're well-suited for potato salad.

examples.japanese: ⟦{北海道|ほっかいどう}→北海道：11010_hokkaidou⟧{産|さん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{男爵|だんしゃく}いも⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{全国的|ぜんこくてき}→全国的：20017_zenkokuteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧で、⟦{特|とく}に→特に：01260_tokuni⟧⟦{秋|あき}→秋：02276_aki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{収穫期|しゅうかくき}→収穫期：21343_shuukakuki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧いも{掘|ほ}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しむ→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧。
examples.english: Baron potatoes from Hokkaido are famous nationwide, and especially during the autumn harvest many people enjoy potato digging.

notes:
PEERAGE RANKS:
The five ranks of Japanese peerage ({華族|かぞく}), from highest to lowest:
- ⟦{公爵|こうしゃく}→公爵：17797_koushaku⟧: duke/prince
- {侯爵|こうしゃく}: marquis
- ⟦{伯爵|はくしゃく}→伯爵：11721_hakushaku⟧: count/earl
- {子爵|ししゃく}: viscount
- {男爵|だんしゃく}: baron

POTATO USAGE:
In everyday conversation, {男爵|だんしゃく} often refers to the potato variety rather than the noble title. The contrast pair in Japanese cooking is {男爵|だんしゃく} (floury, good for mashing) vs. メークイン (waxy, good for simmering).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {男爵|だんしゃく}⟦{夫人|ふじん}→夫人：03597_fujin⟧: baroness
- {男爵|だんしゃく}いも: baron potato (Irish Cobbler)
- {男爵|だんしゃく}{家|け}: baronial family
